text: We are often told that a good life means more, more money, more followers, more stuff, and so we are made to feel lazy or simple if we say that we are happy with what we have. But in my experience, the happiest people are those who don't constantly chase more. They cherish what they have. They find something great wherever they are. I've spent most of my life studying the best and worst ideas in philosophy, and I think I'm ready to share the philosophy that I live by. And so I've written the book, is called the art of enough, and it's about Epicurianism. Epicurus was an ancient Greek philosopher who spent his life studying why it is that some people are so restless while some people are also happy. I've always been an anxious person, but Epicurianism helped me find peace, and I hope it helps you too. My book is a medicine in four parts. First, it says that philosophy is important, because Epicurus told his students that they should introspect. We should listen to our feelings and what they tell us, but we should also have deep and important conversations with our friends. Second, we should wrestle back control of our lives. We need to savor what gives us joy in life and work out how to resolve what makes us anxious and gives us pain. We need to make better decisions. Third, we should take our relationships far more seriously. Epicurus said that of all of the things that wisdom provides to make us truly happy, the greatest is friendship. To be happy, we need to love and to be loved often. Finally, we need to commit to fewer things. Epicurians were the original anti-hustle philosophers. They argued that we should do less, but do more of what we are good at, what we enjoy, and we should aim to become a local legend in the small patch of lands that we call home.
